title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Noble Village Board met in regular session Tuesday night.

The Board approved the payment of bills and heard an update on the nuisance case for a specific property along West North Avenue with the next court date set for June 16th.  They were updated on a water leak found on North First Street.  The landowner is waiting for a plumber to show up and do the work. And, the Water Superintendent gave a list to the clerk for the residents that have grass or weeds taller than 8”.  The Clerk has sent letters to each one on the list.

Clerk Cindy Manuel stated that she is currently scheduled to work 35 hours per week.  Due to being new to the position, additional time is sometimes required to complete tasks and conduct necessary research.  The Board discussed allowing the Clerk to work additional hours as needed.  The board voted to limit the Clerk’s hours to not exceed 40 hours per pay period.

Residents were reminded that the Freedom Festival and parade will be held in the Noble Park on Saturday, June 27th.

The next regular meeting for the Noble Village Board will be June 8th.

title: HOUSE PASSES RESOLUTIONS IN HONOR
full_story:
The Illinois House of Representatives Thursday approved Senate Joint Resolutions in honor and memory of two Effingham area natives who died in service of our country.

The House approved resolutions honoring Sergeant Timothy Sayne and Chief Warrant Officer 2 Christopher Donaldson.  Both resolutions were approved 113-0, and both were approved earlier by the Illinois Senate.

The Fayette Avenue overpass will be named the Sgt. Timothy Sayne Memorial Overpass.  The 4th Street overpass in Effingham will be named the Chief Warrant Officer 2 Christopher Donaldson Memorial Overpass.

State Representative Blaine Wilhour of Beecher City was chief sponsor of the House resolution honoring Donaldson, while State Representative Adam Niemerg of Dieterich was the chief sponsor of the resolution honoring Sayne.  State Senator Steve McClure of Springfield was the chief sponsor for both resolutions in the Illinois Senate.  State Senators Jason Plummer and Chapin Rose co-sponsored both of the resolutions in the Senate.

Chief Warrant Officer Donaldson was assigned to the 3rd Battalion, 10th Aviation Regiment, 10th Mountain Division (Light Infantry), out of Ft. Drum, New York.  Donaldson died May 5th, 2006 when the CH-47 Chinook helicopter he was traveling on crashed during combat operations east of Abad, Afghanistan.

Sergeant Sayne began serving in the US Army in 2008.  He was stationed in Alaska and was assigned to B Troop, 5-1 Calvary, 1/25 Stryker Brigade Combat Team, 25th Infantry Division.  Sayne was killed in action during an insurgent attack in Shah Wali Kot in Kandahar Province, Afghanistan on September 18, 2011.

The Illinois Department of Transportation was requested to create appropriate signage in recognition of Donaldson and Sayne.

Pictured are Chief Warrant Officer 2 Christopher Donaldson, and Sergeant Timothy Sayne.

title: SPRING TURKEY SEASON
full_story:
Illinois hunters harvested a preliminary record total of 20,821 wild turkeys during the 2026 spring turkey season, surpassing the previous record of 18,189 birds harvested in 2025.

In our area Clay County hunters took 105 more turkeys than last year with a total of 398 birds.  Marion County hunters took 530 turkeys this year compared to 428 last year.  Wayne County hunters took 464 turkeys compared to 404 last year.  Fayette County hunters harvested 447 birds compared to 386 last year.  Effingham County hunters took 215 compared to 190 last year and Richland County hunters harvested 139 compared to 158 last year.

The top counties for turkey harvest during the 2026 season were Jefferson and Jo Daviess counties, tied with 646 birds harvested; followed by Marion, 530; Pike, 525; and Wayne, 464.

This year, hunters purchased 94,704 permits compared to 89,580 last year.  This year’s total included a record youth spring turkey season harvest of 2,326 birds compared to 2,099 birds in 2025.

A total of 70,158 individual hunters purchased permits for the 2026 spring turkey season.  Preliminary figures indicate approximately 22% of permits sold were filled this year, compared to 20.3% last year.

Spring turkey hunting was open in 100 of Illinois’ 102 counties. The 2026 regular season dates were April 6th through May 7th in the south zone and April 13th through May 14th in the north zone.  The youth spring turkey season was held March 28th and 29th and April 4th and 5th statewide.

title: FROG ISLAND TENNIS CAMP
full_story:
The Frog Island Tennis Camp starts on Monday.  Flora High School Tennis Coach Daniel Pieplow says the camp will run each day weather permitting through Friday, at the Kayo Powless Tennis Courts.

This year incoming 9th through 12th graders will have camp from 8:30 to 9:30 am; 2nd through 5th grade will have camp from 9:30 to 10:30, and incoming 6th through 8th graders will have camp from 10:30 to 11:30 am.

Cost of the Camp is $30 for the first family member and $25 for additional family members.  Sign-ups will be held on the first day of the camp at the tennis courts and you’ll need an entry form for each camper.

If you have questions about the camp you can call Daniel Pieplow at 618-676-5539 or Jerry Stringer at 618-662-2963.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross is asking you to donate blood as we head toward the summer months.  The organization says there is traditionally more of a need at this time of year and all blood types are needed, especially Type O, which can be used when a patient’s blood type is unknown.

There is a blood drive Monday, from 1 to 6 pm at the Clay Electric Coop.  Donors will receive a $15 gift card by email.

Then there will be a Blood Drive at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church on Tuesday, June 9th from Noon to 6 pm.  After that the next Blood Drive will be on Thursday, June 11th from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).

title: CHAMBER GOLF SCRAMBLE POSTPONED
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce has postponed their 28th annual golf scramble to Friday, August 14th.

The Chamber will be offering a variety of sponsorship opportunities to suit every budget up until the event.  From Gold Sponsorship at $400 to the affordable Bronze Sponsorship at $50, there’s an option for everyone to get involved and showcase their support for the Flora business community.

Team registration is $50 per person or $200 per team.  Entry fee includes 4 drink tickets courtesy of the Flora Bank and Trust a goodie bag with a sleeve of balls and lunch courtesy of the Flora Savings Bank.  There will also be mulligans, 4 foot strings, and yellow tee boxes, for $20 each or $50 for all 3.

Check-in will begin at 11:30 am inside the Clubhouse, lunch is at Noon, and tee-time at 1:00pm on the day of the tournament.

To register your team call Arriel Dulaney at the Flora Chamber of Commerce at 618-662-5646.

title: HARVEST FOR ALL
full_story:
Collegiate Farm Bureau and Illinois FFA chapters throughout the state are making a measurable impact in their communities.

Through Farm Bureau’s Harvest for All program, the youth and collegiate students collected 68,577.85 pounds of food, volunteered 13,142.16 hours and raised $76,645.23, meeting a wide range of local needs.  Combined with the Illinois Farm Bureau Young Leaders program, their efforts contribute to IFB’s statewide Harvest for All total, which surpassed $233,000 raised in 2025.

“Harvest for All made us feel like we were able to give back and know that all of the efforts were actually doing something substantial in our community,” said Janella Neary, who was the University of Illinois Collegiate Farm Bureau member services and programming coordinator during the 2025-26 school year.

The U of I Collegiate Farm Bureau chapter won the collegiate competition this year, raising $1,500 and donating nearly 2,000 pounds of food to the Eastern Illinois Foodbank in Urbana.  The other two top chapters were Kaskaskia College in Centralia and Lincoln Land Community College in Springfield.

Chapters in the Illinois Association FFA also participated in their own Harvest for All contest, competing within their respective sections.  Section winners were selected in each of Illinois FFA’s 25 sections based on their service efforts, with five chapters named as overall winners.

“Whether organizing food drives, packing meals, raising funds for local causes or serving their communities in countless other ways, these students stepped up to make a difference while living out the FFA motto, ‘Living to Serve,’” IFB Youth and Collegiate Program Coordinator Taylor Hartke said.  “Harvest for All captures the impact of students who move beyond words and put service into action.”
